As some who put in hours into this game, I can confirm that the game starts out slow and boring. Everything feels underwhelming; The drop rates, the grind, super weak and underpowered descendants, underperforming weapons and lackluster combat with the 3 basic descendants. However, after you’ve built up the mods for your character and weapon and pay attention to the minute details such as weapon elemental damage types and resistances, the game becomes SO MUCH FUN. If you have experience in warframe, you should be able to dive right in as the mechanics for build crafting are very similar. Now I am not F2P but the game is f2p friendly however, it requires soooo much grinding. I love the game so I don’t mind supporting the developers. This is a game that on the surface is trash but once you invest the time, and maybe some money if you can, it becomes worth every second. I hate Nexon for their shady ToS practices but I love The First Descendant.

 I will add, the game needs some QoL fine tuning and I’ve been giving my requests to the first descendant team on discord (respectfully!) hopefully the changes get implemented.

 One issue to note is they designed certain activities to throttle our farming grind and in a looter shooter game, that is very annoying. But this is just a personal opinion, not a QoL change :)

As someone who played both the Steam Beta and Cross Play test, I wanted to love this game so bad, but I just can't.

The monetization is just so horrible that it makes the game nigh unplayable.

For the sake of my sanity, as a 5k hour Warframe veteran, I will be comparing those 2 directly.

The core of the game is almost exactly like Warframe (collecting and upgrading different characters and weapons) with the mission design being similar to that of Destiny / Anthem.

1 Descendant costs anywhere from 300-900 Caliber (Premium Currency), which is roughly $10-20, because $5 only gets you 250 Caliber. Bear in mind that these Descendants DO NOT COME WITH THE ITEM THAT INCREASES BASE MOD CAPACITY PRE-INSTALLED! This also applies to the Ultimate Descendants that cost anywhere between $69.99 (this bundle only includes the Descendant, a Descendant slot, and a skin) and $99.99 (this bundle includes all of the $69.99 bundle content as well as a pre-built Activator and 2 Shape Stabilizers to both increase the capacity of the Descendant and get started on a build).

In Warframe, if you BUY a Warframe with Platinum (Premium Currency), they come with an Orokin Reactor to increase mod capacity pre-installed... That Orokin Reactor costs 20 Platinum, or less than $2 when you do the math.

The Activator that increases mod capacity in TFD... WILL COST YOU $50 MINIMUM! AND IF YOU WANT TO FARM IT, IT HAS A MINUSCULE 3% BASE DROP CHANCE FOR A BLUEPRINT THAT YOU THEN NEED TO FARM ALL OF THE MATERIALS FOR!

And you need 1 of them for every Descendant (character) and weapon that you want to use regularly.

On top of that, this game's Forma equivalent (the material that allows you to change gear polarities to fit more mods by reducing mod costs) is almost as bad in terms of drop rate (15% for a blueprint) and costs the same as a "vanilla" Descendant at 300 Caliber, or $10. For ONE single item.

The equivalent item in Warframe is easily farmed, because they have a very high drop rate from their F2P drop source (relics) and they are the exact same price as an Orokin Reactor at less than $2 / unit... and they can be purchased in bundles of 3 for 35 Platinum (just over $2).

There is a good game here, it's just so egregiously and aggressively monetized that it actively hinders gameplay progress and enjoyment.

Is it POSSIBLE to go through entirely F2P? Yes.

Is it worth your time and effort to do so? Absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ not.

If you want a sci-fi looter shooter, just go play Warframe, because unlike this game, it actually respects your time, effort, and money if you choose to spend it.

If you need any more proof of that fact, consider that the "compensation" for the day 1 issues and multiple server outages in the first 3-4 days was 6 days worth of +30% boosters for XP and currency gain.

Nothing like Activators, "Forma", or anything useful for new players.

Just boosters that make the grind 30% less annoying.

While the gameplay is good in the first descendant, the amount of predatory monetization at work here is INSANE. 

1. Unlocking descendants: While you can grind these champions out, there is also a method to just straight up by them. This is pretty normal until you realize that some of these bundles cost $100. FOR ONE CHARACTER. I played for 6  hours straight and only unlocked 2 descendants. Ajax, who I chose at the beginning of the game for free, and Bunny, who was essentially free and given to you at level 10. I am NOWHERE near unlocking any of the other champions. Too much of it is RNG based, inevitably you will end up with lots of small puzzle pieces needed for each champion but still not even have enough for one complete unlock. 

2. Battle Pass: Damn, I thought Overwatch 2 and Call of Duty had the worst battle passes in the industry but holy hell did The First Descendant obliterate the competition. 
- No operator skins. How do you get this wrong? nobody buys a battle pass because of weapons or funny knick-knacks. Not even one? seriously?
- ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ new currency taking up space. You get this exclusive store that requires you to purchase items using a new special currency found in the premium battle pass that isn't caliber(the currency used to buy the BP). This is like radianite in Valorant except worse because the items in the special shop are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. 
- Rebuys aren't free. ♥♥♥♥ you, thats why. 
- Confusing rewards. theres like one gun in the battlepass that shows up like 5 times. I don't even know what to say. 
- Grindiness. I played for SIX. HOURS. and got ONE tier. 

3. Caliber: The conversion rate for caliber is 1 Caliber for $2 USD. This means that in contrary to popular trends amongst games, an item in the shop costing 250 caliber costs $5 USD, not 2.50. Clearly this is yet another method at trying to get you into thinking an item is cheaper than it actually is. Why else would they not stick to the normal 1:1 ratio? This item in the shop costing 5000 caliber? must be 50 bucks. SIKE!!! it's actually $100!!! Call people who fall for this stupid if you want but this is so obviously just another ploy to try and nudge you closer and closer to buying an item. 

As of this review, there is no way to get Caliber for free. Also happens that cosmetics are locked exclusively behind Caliber. So, even if you just wanted a teeny tiny item costing 75 caliber or so, TOO BAD! you have to spend money. Yet another strategy meant to get consumers to make their first purchase. 

4. Shameless stealing? Really? 
Besides stealing it's inspirations' ♥♥♥♥♥♥ monetization models, some descendants are straight ripped from other IPs. The guide here is basically from destiny 2. Bunny? more like Neon from Valorant smashed with DVA's personality. Viessa? more like Ciri's long lost retarted cousin with 0 points invested in the modesty stat. FREYNA HAS TO BE THE MOST BOLD FACED VIPER COPY I HAVE EVER SEEN. Just stop bro even the name of the hub world, Albion, isn't original. 

Personally I think if you are media aware and can recognize the signs of predatory marketing than you can play this game completely f2p and have a blast. I did, it was tons of fun. But I cannot support a game like this which takes every single predatory marketing strategy seen in the last 10 years of gaming and lumps them into a single release. This game is looking to piggyback off of Destiny 2's success and now-finished story line, looking to be the next big looter shooter. Please don't let this be the next standard for gaming. 


Lastly, I know this game has boobs and ass but please show some restraint and cognizance and recognize the flaws that lie underneath this gold-plated turd.

Do not waste your time on this game—it's a Looter Shooter that blatantly copies Warframe, with a few elements from Destiny 2, designed solely to extract money from players. 

TLDR: This company is known for throwing games out there for 1/2 years, raking in the money and then shutting down servers; do not invest your time in this game if you expect to be F2P, you will fall behind.

The game's UI is cluttered, the movement is clunky, and there's a significant input delay that isn't even server-related; it's inherent to the game. Numerous clipping issues reported during Beta tests were ignored, yet the in-game shop is brimming with new cosmetics!

The worst aspect is the monetisation. The premium currency cannot be earned or traded, is vastly overpriced, and this is unlikely to change. The gameplay is unremarkable and not worth your time. Some players claim that the complaints come from those unwilling to 'grind'; this isn't true. The game puts down substantial barriers, forcing you to either continuously struggle against them or spend real money to get the desired Descendant/Weapon.

Just because the game is free-to-play, it doesn't mean the monetisation should be this EXPLOITATIVE. Their direct competitor, Warframe, provides a better example—Nexon, take note.

As of writing I have 19.2 hours played here on Steam

I've "level capped" my first descendant and is close to my second one now, all the while farming materials and following the story as I trudge along.
I paid attention to the story last year during the beta, but found it rather forgettable, which is okay, because the focus of this game, and where the fun lies, at least to me, is in the gameplay loop.
The shooting feels really satisfying to me, and the various abilities feel impactful and fun to use (if a bit undertuned in some cases).

The game plays abit like how I remember Destiny being (not D2, the OG one) where you roam an open world map with various objectives on it, alongside other people, you then start missions located around on the map, and sometimes random people will join you, and sometimes they wont, with a properly geared character I haven't had any issues taking on any of the map encounters on my own so far, they seem to be tuned for solo play.

The fun parts are the instanced areas to me, where you go into a mini dungeon with a boss at the end. There are also some other game modes, iirc from the beta, which I haven't touched yet, and then the big bosses, which to me are the most challenging, at the point I am at in the game I have defeated 4 of them, with I think 5 more to go, and then there's also hard modes of each of them. The big baddies (I really dont remember what they're actually called) are huge bosses you fight in a boss arena together with 3 other people, and you really have to be on your toes to win, since there's a 10 minute timer and a respawn limit.

All in all I think this game shows promise, I personally think the skins are too expensive, and the fact that dyes are not re-usable is kinda rough, but it is perfectly possible to play the game entirely for free, and still do all the content with being gatekept.
There is also a seasonal battle pass, which currently is 5 euros worth of their premium currency, for a whole lot of unlocks that you get as you play, the battle pass also has a free option, with far fewer rewards. As of now I have not spend any money, but I am considering maybe giving the battle pass a go, since I am having so much fun with the game.

tl;dr
If you like Warframe and Destiny, then there's a lot of stuff here you might find enjoyable, I personally aren't too fond of either of those games, and I still love this one, so maybe give it a go, even if you aren't a warframe/destiny 2 enjoyer :)

The First Descendant is a third person looter shooter co-op style RPG game, were you play as Descendants who have inherited power from the Ancestors and are trying to stop the world from being taken over by an evil forces.

The Good 

From the jump this game takes elements from many other titles that make it feel like a classic looter shooter that people know and love. From Warframe to Destiny this game features many fun and interesting aspects of character and weapon building and has a decent story to go along with it. I enjoy the open world combat and missions as well as, being able to switch up descendants and try new things. The Sci-Fi style world makes the enemies and abilities really fun to fight and explore. There is always something to do in this game no matter what your style of play is which is something you don't always see in games today. Game play and graphics feel smooth and beautiful. Also the optimization is well done and doesn't hold this game back from being what it is. Only 14 hours in and I still feel like coming back for more. 

The Bad

This being a Nexon game the micro transactions are a bit of an issue but you don't need them to really enjoy this game which is good. The bugs have been an issue the first couple days everything from audio, combat and even just going from one area to the next can be bothersome. Story could be a bit better after a while it just feels like the same old same old but all depends on your preferences at the the end of the day. One thing I would like is better is the fact that a lot of things feel generic in many ways such as missions other than big boss battles really. Hopefully they change that up down the road but for now it is what it is. 

Overall Thoughts And Score

This game has it all but can also feel like its lacking it key areas. The loot system is not bad but inventory management can be a pain, thankfully after awhile it gets easier. People have many mixed feelings on this game and I can see why I was on the fence about it for a bit, but overall whether solo or co-op its a fun time. One big thing for me was that it's a free to play game so enjoy it for what it is at the end of the day. If your into looter shooters I definitely recommend trying because like iv'e said it takes a lot of its core game from other top titles. 

Score 6.5/10

Warframe but with pretty girls and super-buff dudes (no variation in size. They're all huge dudes despite this being a Korean game). That sounds great but there are some issues:

1. The free way to attain characters and weapons is a huge grind.
2. The prices on the store are horrifying. $20 gets you about 1000 points and a single catalyst (something you can buy in a pack of 3 for about $5 in Warframe) will cost you 800.
3. The builds are much pickier with various types of cards only allowing one type of that card to be equipped. Also, the buffs from cards are also stingy compared to Warframe, so you still work hard but don't become amazing as a result like you can become in Warframe.
4. The character's power kits are trash compared to Warframe. Obviously, Warframe has the advantage of people having leveled up and selected cards to buff builds that work off the frame's powersets, but they just have a lot of them that feel clunky.
5. The writing and story-telling are amateur. They'll use 100 words to say something that could be said in five and they're never clever or witty and only the character "Bunny" seems to have much of a personality or point-of-view so far. The rest are all various flavors of stern soldier - at least so far. The plot points are predictable, the enemy character's motivations are inhuman and cartoonishly evil. There's nothing about this narrative that you can take seriously or enjoy, so it feels like wasted money. All that work and all those voice actors wasted because you couldn't hire one professional writer. 
6. Some of the progression is transparent and fun but unlocking things through research and optimizing cores is unnecessarily complicated and just not fun. You can probably watch a few Youtube videos that explain it and it is likely not that deep or difficult, but good game design doesn't need an expert to teach you how it is actually quite simple and just made complicated by the bad design. This kind of false intricacy is something that mobile game designers do to try to obsfuscate that people are grinding to make numbers go up by miniscule amounts and I wouldn't mind the min/max grind - but I do hate the bad design meant to hide it from dummies.

Is it a terrible game? No. If you don't give them any money, you can have some fun here. I suggest you download it and play it for free. Maybe they'll eventually have enough content that they won't have to make so many silly design choices and/or sell things for ridiculous prices.

A couple of things to understand about this game before you play:

1. IT IS FREE TO PLAY

2. IT'S GONNA HAVE MT's

3. IT WILL TURN INTO A GRIND FEST

4. TAKE YOUR TIME AND DON'T FLY THROUGH THE STORY

Now, with that out of the way, I would honestly give this game 3.5 stars. They'd get a .5 back if there was more content and not just "HARD" mode. 

The lack of PvP and bigger end game activities is hindering the drive behind the grind for better gear. To be more specific when I say "bigger activities" I'm referencing Destiny's Raids or Dungeon like activities. Now, I know everything can't be like other games, but this game is structured SO similarly to warframe and Destiny it's almost like a clone. 

The weird power creeps/HARD power spikes can be daunting. However, the solution isn't just a simple "git gud". It's an RNG based grind for mods (in re-playable story missions/Outposts) and then upgrading them in a warframe style resource dumping (after grinding for it) only to repeat the process for a mod that has a 1% drop rate in a less than engaging mission.

The story is pretty good and mostly creative. However, the bosses and mini bosses kinda start to turn into re-skinned "ok, but now I have 4 shields phases you have to break". A specific instance which I know you probably specifically googled this mfer, "Grunach the Undying". *inhales* *exhales* let me tell you something... NOT ONCE did anything or any mechanic HINT at breaking the "shield orbs" in the order that they spawn. Then just out of the blue while you are cruising through the story, that happens. 

Anyways, I say all this not to scare you off or give them a bad review. I genuinely enjoyed the time I spent playing the game, but there are gonna be some SERIOUS switch ups when people start reaching the end of the story. 

All in all, this game has some aspects that were done VERY well. Gunplay and movement are amazing. The grapple hook takes some practice, but makes moving around big areas a lot of fun. Most characters feel fleshed out and fun to use. Exp gain and leveling feels good. the resource and currency economy isn't too crowded, but feels fleshed out. Honestly for a FtP game It's pretty good. WE JUST NEED MORE ACTIVITIES/ENDGAME CONTENT.

My review will be updated as the game progresses and more content (crossed fingers) is added. It is still in the first season (pre-season? I think) and it's only been out for 5 days.

3.5/5 (will change once more is added)
